researchQuestionText: Can a mechanically perfect, economically rational, legally enforceable peace settlement end the war in Ukraine within the constraints of the current international system?
methodText: On the night between December the 3rd and December the 4th, we used adversarial AI collaboration to iteratively design Protocol Omega—addressing every known diplomatic failure mode through self-executing enforcement, positive-sum economics, and trust-free operation.
resultText: Unanimous rejection by four simulated decision-makers with veto power
conclusionText: Peace is architecturally impossible under current rules
bug1Description: Binary territorial logic makes any ambiguity existentially threatening
bug2Description: Strategic assets are weapons, not commodities—sharing control equals strategic defeat
bug3Description: Great powers optimize for rival disadvantage over absolute stability
bug4Description: Actors profit from instability without penalty
timelineIntro: Quantitative analysis reveals convergent exhaustion across multiple domains:
financialText: Debt service exceeding capacity, crossover points 2028-2035
windowText: 5-10 years for building alternatives before crisis makes preparation impossible
world1Description: System continues until convergent exhaustion. Cascading failures exceed capacity. Fragmentation into warlordism. 150-300 year dark age.
world2Description: Crisis triggers 2030-2038. Alternative architectures ready. Coordinated transition. Post-Westphalian governance by 2050-2060.
world3Description: Technological breakthrough solves scarcity. Psychological evolution enables voluntary constraints. System self-reforms. Structurally implausible.
impactStatement: Each 30-point increase in Preparedness Index = ~5% shift from World 1 → World 2 = 10-15 million lives saved (2035-2050)
researchPackageIntro: Every iteration of Protocol Omega's design and stress-testing, showing the progression from initial concept to bulletproof edition, followed by unanimous rejection. Full transparency on methodology.
ctaText: The experiment is complete. The system is terminal. The work now shifts from negotiation to construction. We have ~5 years to build the replacement kernel.
ctaFooter: The lights will go out. Begin lighting candles.
fallbackNotice: Some sections are displayed in English as Swedish translation is not yet available.
epigraph: This is not a warning. This is a death certificate.
paperSubtitle: An Empirical Demonstration of the Nation-State System's Terminal Incompatibility with Planetary Peace
closingEpigraph: The lights will go out. Begin lighting candles.
endOfPaper: END OF WHITE PAPER | BEGINNING OF SALVAGE
researchPackageDescription: 13 documents showing the evolution from initial concept to unanimous rejection
researchPackageLongDescription: This research package contains the complete, unedited iteration history of the Omega Experiment. Every document, every critique, every refinement—transparent documentation of how we built the most sophisticated peace mechanism possible, and how it was systematically rejected by all four veto players.
synthesisDescription: Generate initial frameworks and conceptual innovations
challengeDescription: Rewrite for realpolitik, execute red team attacks, stress-test mechanics
integrationDescription: Identify vulnerabilities, propose structural improvements, assess feasibility
documentationDescription: Compile findings into rigorous analysis and white paper
readyToDiveDescription: Start from the beginning to see the complete evolution, or jump to any phase that interests you.

revision.noticeTitle: Revision note (September 2026): the conclusion does not hold as stated
revision.noticeText: This page preserves the original December 2025 paper. Its central conclusion, that peace is architecturally impossible under current rules, has been withdrawn. Four AI personas rejecting one proposal cannot show that no acceptable settlement exists. A follow-up research programme reworked the argument and tested it against historical evidence.
revision.sectionTitle: What happened next: from Omega Proof to Omega Constraint
revision.sectionIntro: In September 2026 the paper was put on trial. Every claim was audited, the surviving ideas were formalized, and the formal version was tested against a real peace process. This is a summary of the result.
revision.wrong1: One proposal is not every proposal. Rejection of Protocol Omega shows that this design failed, not that no acceptable settlement exists. Proving impossibility would require searching the whole space of possible agreements, or a genuine impossibility theorem.
revision.wrong2: The AI personas were hardliners explicitly instructed to kill the proposal. That is useful red-teaming: it shows that coherent reasons to reject exist. It does not show how real governments decide.
revision.wrong3: The probabilities, timelines, dark-age durations and lives-saved figures were scenario assumptions presented as calculations. No method in the paper could produce them.
revision.survives1: The mechanisms, as hypotheses rather than laws: territorial and identity salience, commitment credibility, relative-gain concerns and outside actors can each shrink the set of settlements that every veto player finds both acceptable and credible, and together they can sometimes shrink it to nothing.
revision.survives2: A distinction the original erased: 'no acceptable deal exists now' is not the same as 'no institutional path can create one', and neither is the same as 'impossible'. Monitoring, guarantees, phased and partial agreements can change what is feasible.
revision.survives3: Most of this is established bargaining theory (Fearon, Powell, Cunningham, Zartman, Sebenius). Any new contribution would lie in how the pieces are combined and measured, and that remains unproven.
revision.tested1: Pilot case: the Egypt–Israel negotiations from the October 1973 ceasefire to the 1979 peace treaty, reconstructed from the U.S. diplomatic record (Foreign Relations of the United States) under a frozen protocol with preregistered stop/go gates.
revision.tested2: Result: Phase I closed without passing. One of six gates passed. The evidence was almost entirely U.S.-recorded, the AI coders already knew the historical outcome, and the programme produced no dated, falsifiable prediction.
revision.tested3: One documented link was found: Israel accepted monitoring and U.S. assurance arrangements that matched concerns its negotiators had stated. That is one case, below the preregistered threshold, and not confirmation of the theory.
revision.learned1: Parties may distrust the mediator as much as each other. In the 1975 Sinai talks, the recorded credibility concerns were mostly about U.S. backing, not only about the other side.
revision.learned2: Summaries of proposals lose the reasons behind positions. Reasons must be extracted first, or constraints like credibility disappear from the data.
revision.learned3: AI-assisted research needs genuinely independent checks: repeated runs of one model are not independent coders, and models that know how history ended cannot make blind forecasts.
revision.statusWithdrawn: Withdrawn: peace is impossible under current rules; the four 'terminal bugs' as laws of the system; all probabilities, timelines and casualty figures.
revision.statusRetained: Retained as hypotheses: the four mechanisms; the distinction between current, reachable and bounded infeasibility.
revision.statusOpen: Not established: that this framing adds anything beyond existing bargaining theory.
revision.closing: The original paper follows unchanged, as a record of the argument and the method that produced it.
revision.ctaText: The experiment did not show that the system is terminal or that peace is impossible. It surfaced hypotheses about why settlements fail and how institutions can open space for them, and those hypotheses are now being tested with more honest methods.
revision.ctaFooter: Kept online as a record of a claim, its critique and its correction.
revision.shortNoticeTitle: This is an archived paper with a withdrawn conclusion
revision.whitePaperNotice: This is the original December 2025 text, preserved unchanged. Its central claim, that peace is architecturally impossible under current rules, was withdrawn in September 2026, along with its probabilities, timelines and casualty figures. The mechanisms it describes survive only as hypotheses.
revision.visualsNotice: These diagrams illustrate the original December 2025 paper. Its impossibility conclusion has been withdrawn, and the probabilities, timelines and preparedness effects shown here were scenario assumptions without a calibration method. Treat them as illustrations of the original argument, not as findings.
revision.researchNotice: These are the unedited AI working documents behind the original paper. The 'rejections' were produced by AI personas instructed to act as hardliners and kill the proposal: they show that coherent reasons to reject exist, not how real governments would decide. The paper's impossibility conclusion has since been withdrawn.
